title: Introduction to Node.js
description: Learn what Node.js is, its history, features, and why it has become a popular runtime environment for JavaScript outside the browser.

lessons.title: What is Node.js?
lessons.content: Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform runtime environment that allows developers to run JavaScript on the server side. It is built on Chrome's V8 JavaScript engine and enables scalable network applications.

lessons.title: History and Evolution of Node.js
lessons.content: Node.js was created by Ryan Dahl in 2009 to build scalable network applications. It introduced an event-driven, non-blocking I/O model that made it efficient and suitable for data-intensive real-time applications.

lessons.title: Key Features of Node.js
lessons.content:
- Asynchronous and Event-Driven
- Single-threaded but highly scalable
- Fast execution with V8 engine
- Rich ecosystem with npm (Node Package Manager)
- Suitable for real-time applications like chat and gaming

lessons.title: Why Use Node.js?
lessons.content: Node.js allows developers to use JavaScript for both client and server-side code, which simplifies development. It excels in building fast, scalable network applications and is widely used in modern web development.

lessons.title: Overview of Node.js Architecture
lessons.content: Node.js uses a single-threaded event loop architecture to handle concurrent connections efficiently. This design avoids traditional thread-based concurrency and allows high throughput.
